summary.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation

details: RLVR post-training is expensive because the target model must generate rollouts, so re-running it for every new, larger model becomes the bottleneck; running RL on a cheap small model and then distilling its final post-RL policy fails because that policy entangles RL gains with the weak model's capacity ceiling (it can drag down students that already beat the teacher).

Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD): instead of matching a post-RL teacher's distribution, it transfers the teacher's RL-induced policy shift, the log-ratio log pi_T - log pi_T_ref between a post-RL weak checkpoint and its own pre-RL reference, treated as a dense per-token implicit reward.

Justified by the KL-regularized-RL/DPO identity read in reverse: the policy-reference log-ratio equals the latent reward up to positive scale and a per-prompt constant, so a checkpoint pair stores RL supervision in policy space.

The signal is evaluated on the student's own on-policy states over its top-k support (Rao-Blackwellized, stop-gradient-weighted token-level policy gradient), regularized by KL to the student's own initialization with a sign-of-reward adaptive KL coefficient controller.

Teacher pairs: R1-Distill-1.5B -> JustRL-1.5B; Nemotron-1.5B -> QuestA-Nemotron-1.5B (different pipeline/data); plus own GRPO RL checkpoints of R1-Distill-1.5B on DAPO data at steps 300/600/900/1200/1500 and a 100-step Qwen3-1.7B-nonthinking run.
Students: R1-Distill-7B, Qwen3-1.7B, Qwen3-4B (7B and 4B start above the post-RL JustRL teacher), plus Qwen3-4B-nonthinking.
verl framework; Skywork-OR1-RL-Data math subset (similar trends with DAPO-Math-17K), DAPO-style prompt template.
Global batch 64, rollout n=4, max prompt 1024, max response 2048 (short 2k horizon), temperature 1.0, lr 1e-6, 300 steps, student top-k support k=16.
KL coefficient fixed in [0.8, 2] per pair, or adaptive controller (eps=0.01, alpha in [0.5, 2.5]).
Transfer cost: about 4 hours on 8 A100 GPUs.
Vanilla on-policy distillation toward the post-RL teacher.
Direct GRPO RL on the large target (R1-Distill-7B, Qwen3-4B-nonthinking; batch 512/128, rollout n=8, response 16k, KL 0), compared at matched RL steps and matched wall-clock.
Reference point: Polaris RL directly on Qwen3-1.7B (32 A100s, ~1 week).
AIME 2024 and AIME 2025, 32 samples per problem (ave@32), temperature 0.7, top-p 0.95, max generation 31,744 tokens.
Response-length sweep (2k/4k/6k) with a prefix cumulative teacher-gap diagnostic G_T over 64 fixed long (~16k) rollouts.
Fixed-KL sweep versus adaptive KL, tracking dense token reward and validation accuracy.
Teacher-student top-k overlap (against both post-RL teacher and reference) and actor/teacher entropy diagnostics.
Sequential composition of two policy shifts in one student.

key_findings.finding: Transferring a weak teacher's RL-induced policy shift improves students that are already stronger than the post-RL teacher, where imitating the teacher's final policy hurts.
key_findings.evidence: From R1-Distill-7B (56.7 on AIME24, above the 51.3 post-RL JustRL-1.5B teacher), vanilla OPD toward that teacher falls to roughly 50, while Direct-OPD rises to 63.1 (AIME25 40.5 -> 48.8); Qwen3-4B improves 72.5 -> 77.6 and Qwen3-1.7B 48.3 -> 58.3 on AIME24, with the second teacher pair (QuestA-Nemotron) giving +10.7 on Qwen3-1.7B and +4.9 on R1-Distill-7B, indicating the effect is not tied to one teacher pipeline.

key_findings.finding: Running RL on a small model and transferring the shift beats direct RL on the large target at matched RL steps and at far lower compute.
key_findings.evidence: Transfers from 1.5B RL checkpoints T600-T1500 into R1-Distill-7B sit above the direct 7B RL curve on AIME 2025 at comparable elapsed time; 1500-step RL costs ~160 h on 32 A100s for the 1.5B versus ~320 h for the 7B, with the Direct-OPD stage adding only ~4 h on 8 A100s; transferring a 100-step Qwen3-1.7B shift into Qwen3-4B-nonthinking reaches the 0.635 direct-RL accuracy on AIME 2025.

key_findings.finding: Independently learned policy shifts can be composed sequentially in the same student, accumulating gains.
key_findings.evidence: Qwen3-1.7B trained first with the R1-Distill-1.5B -> JustRL-1.5B shift then continued with the Nemotron -> QuestA shift goes 48.3 -> 58.3 -> 63.8 on AIME24 and 36.8 -> 43.2 -> 46.8 on AIME25.

key_findings.finding: Unlike standard OPD, the transfer does not proceed via progressive imitation of the teacher's high-probability tokens.
key_findings.evidence: In cross-pattern transfers, student top-k overlap with the post-RL teacher stays low with no compensating rise in overlap with the reference, yet accuracy improves; actor entropy does not collapse (while the teacher-reference entropy gap narrows), for both JustRL and QuestA teacher pairs.
